articles.title: ‘I’ve got more of a sense of humour than Ralph Lauren’ – nine things we learned from Paul Smith’s new memoir
articles.summary: He put personality into boxers, collaborated with the pope (sort of) and is to thank for novelty socks. The British designer’s new book reveals there’s more to Smith than his stripes.
body: I n July, the British designer Paul Smith celebrated his 80th birthday and he has now released a memoir to mark the occasion. Threads: My Life in Style tells Smith’s story, from growing up in Nottingham and leaving school with no qualifications to selling suits to celebs, including Gary Oldman and David Bowie.

1. He made boxers something you want to be seen in In the 70s, Smith reimagined boxers in clashing prints and colours, such as polka dots and stripes rather than drab greys and whites, catapulting them from the back of the underwear drawer to the pages of fashion magazines. “I always describe my early success as nudging rather than shoving the British male into appreciating the fact that you could be a little different,” he writes.
points: He put personality into boxers, collaborated with the pope (sort of) and is to thank for novelty socks.

articles.title: A scientist said bananas ‘kill’ the benefit of blueberries. Is that true?
articles.summary: Can blending these popular fruits in a smoothie adversely affect the berries’ nutritional benefits? Experts weigh in. This year was shaping up to be a banner year for bananas: they were lauded as “ 2026’s big viral taste ”, landed pride of place as Prada’s new lip balm flavor, and were even deemed…
body: But this summer, the Mel Robbins Podcast featured Dr Rhonda Patrick, a biomedical scientist, who said that adding banana to a blueberry smoothie could adversely affect the nutritional benefits of the berries.
Could the beloved mashup of blueberries and bananas really be a bad match?

Patrick’s claim involved an enzyme called polyphenol oxidase, which appears in bananas, and polyphenols, an umbrella term for a diverse family of antioxidant compounds found in plants – including blueberries.

“Polyphenol oxidase, it’s essentially an enzyme that’s breaking down the polyphenols. And there have now been studies … showing if you add bananas to blueberries, you’re not getting as many polyphenols. In fact, it’s quite a bit lower. So the banana is killing the benefit,” she said.

articles.title: Ralph Lauren proves the American dream still sells at New York fashion week
articles.summary: Designer mixes burnt-out velvet and shredded denim with a mythology that keeps getting more profitable. The opening show of fashion’s month of catwalks was not on the official schedule, but Viola Davis and Cynthia Erivo were snuggled on to celebrity-packed benches in a cathedral-sized marble hall…
body: Ralph Lauren, 86, took his bow at the end of this women’s wear show casually dressed in a varsity jacket spelling out New York. In an industry obsessed with youth and novelty, Lauren is more relevant than ever in his ninth decade.

He described the show as “irreverent”. Velvet evening wear was burnt out to show a little skin beneath. There were shredded, low-slung jeans – take note, jeans-wearers everywhere – and a wink to the extra-wide ties that started his empire 59 years ago.
The spray-painted brocade gowns and lush embroidered evening coats on this catwalk will be giddily expensive, but the energy propelling the brand comes from a much broader audience.

Gen Z has rediscovered Ralph Lauren, and its Polo shirts, rugby shirts and baseball caps are cool again, a renaissance that shows up emphatically on the balance sheet. This year the fashion house reached its highest ever annual revenue figure of $8.1bn (£6bn) – a rise of 15% on the previous year.
points: Designer mixes burnt-out velvet and shredded denim with a mythology that keeps getting more profitable.

articles.title: ‘Adults’ Is the Gen Z Comedy Making Me, a Millennial, Feel Optimistic
articles.summary: “It’s silly but well-acted, puerile but clever, and I defy you not to come away charmed by these characters,” Jessica Barrett writes. “It’s laugh-out-loud funny, but doesn’t try too hard to impart lessons. It’s my favorite comedy of the year.”
body: Only “Mr. Teacher,” as the group has christened him, has taken enough ketamine to take out an army. The chicken is raw. Julia Fox, guest-starring as herself, vows never, ever to return to Queens, where the friends are squatting in Samir’s family home while his parents are travelling. The night ends on a glum note of acceptance: they don’t have their lives together at all.

Traces of the DNA of Girls, which offered something more raw and real for millennial viewers a decade after Friends went off the air, can also be found in Adults, which mines the inevitable humiliations of 20-something hedonism for its comedy. But while those hapless heroines embodied the Girl Boss energy and hustle culture of the 2010s—Hannah Horvath had her heart set on being the voice of her generation, while Marnie longed to be a musical sensation—career aspirations rarely factor in Adults. The workplace does not hold the magic they seek, which is true to life: recent stats found that 49% of Gen Z views work as central to their identity, compared to 62% of millennials.

articles.title: Inside the Buzziest Parties of New York Fashion Week
articles.summary: Beyond the runways and presentations, the Spring 2027 season has also spelled no shortage of parties popping off across Manhattan—with plenty of celebrity names on the guest lists too. Here, Vogue’s look inside the events everyone is still talking about…
body: In SoHo’s hotspot Raoul’s, an assembly of well-known faces gathered over steak and stripes for one reason: a celebration of Banana Republic and La Ligne’s new collaboration. And what better place to spotlight the coming together of an American heritage brand and a French-inspired label than in this beloved bistro? It just made sense, much like the pieces in the collection. Both parties center their designs around effortless everyday dressing, and this synergy was exemplified in the co-created line of smooth nubuck barn coats, perfectly-cut corduroy pants, transitional shell trenches, and, of course, impeccably striped sweaters.

Naturally, every guest clad in the collection looked effortlessly polished. Zoey Deutch, the face of the campaign, giggled with Zac Posen over dirty martinis. Rachel Brosnahan and Zazie Beetz laughed as the trio of La Ligne founders—Valerie Macaulay, Meredith Melling, and Molly Howard—joked: “The only complaint of this whole collaboration is that the shopping bags aren’t big enough to take it all home!” —Gaby Keiderling.

articles.title: In Utah’s Mountains, a Self-Help Skeptic Learns to Open Up
articles.summary: At a retreat in The Lodge at Blue Sky, learning that wellbeing comes in all its forms—from unplugging on an afternoon hike to spilling out feelings at a sweat lodge.
body: I’m sitting on the ground in a completely dark teepee, sweat dripping from every pore. The Shoshone chief next to me pours more water on the hot stones that are stacked in the middle of our circle of ten. There’s a hiss, then steam rises up with nowhere to escape, filling the space. Chief Darren Parry tells us a word, a prompt. One by one, we share. I’d planned to pass. But when it’s my turn, I find myself spilling out feelings I’d never shared with anyone—barely let myself even think about—with strangers I’d met less than 48 hours prior.

When the invitation came—to attend a wellness retreat in the mountains of Utah—I jumped at the chance. I’d been toying with the idea of a yoga retreat for months, and while this wasn’t exactly that (yoga was on the itinerary for just one morning), it was close enough to feel serendipitous. I couldn’t wait to get back out West, but the skeptic in me tempered my expectations.

articles.title: Alo Kicked Off NYFW with a Chic Night at The Twenty Two
articles.summary: To usher in New York Fashion Week and simultaneously unveil the second collection of high-end handbags, Alo hosted a dinner party and late-night bash at The Twenty Two.
body: Ahead of a family-style meal, Candice Swanepoel, Amelia Gray Hamlin, and Daiane Sodre, who once again front the latest glossy campaign by Steven Meisel, this time alongside Natasha Poly and Ming Xi, reunited on the ninth floor of the elegant hotel. While their form-fitting athleisure had been swapped for more PM-appropriate outfits—the crystal-adorned leather bags still remained tucked under their arms.

Welcoming guests—who also included The Shards star Hayes Warner, Winnie Harlow, and Delilah Belle Hamlin, Alo’s longtime EVP of marketing and creative, Summer Barry Nacewicz, reflected on the road to now. “Alo actually started back in 2007—it’s been a really long journey, and we’ve always done things differently,” she said. “Where most athletic brands would never come out with a handbag, last year, we set out to make the nicest bags possible—all made in Italy with excellent craftsmanship.”

articles.title: All That Glimmers: Hailee Steinfeld and Estée Lauder Unveiled their New Fragrance
articles.summary: Hailee Steinfeld hosted an intimate West Village launch for Glimmer, the first gourmand fragrance from Estée Lauder built around life's fleeting joys.
body: On Wednesday evening, in the calm before the chaos of NYFW, sight, sound, and scent came together at the launch party of Estée Lauder’s new eau de parfum, Glimmer, hosted alongside its campaign star, Hailee Steinfeld.

The Oscar-nominated multi-hyphenate was all smiles when describing how she fell in love with the evocative fragrance. “It’s a feeling first, and then a memory, and future memories, and also what I wanted it to represent for me at this moment in my life,” she told Vogue.

Since becoming a first-time mom months ago, the Sinners actress added, “I now love the idea of putting emphasis on these small daily pockets of joy that we all experience: like getting into clean sheets at the end of the day, or seeing your baby smile. It reminds me that life is so beautiful and it moves so fast, and I just loved the thought that this is a scent that one day my little girl will associate me with and how that will become a cherished memory for her.”

articles.title: 19 Margarita Recipes for Any Season
articles.summary: Like spicy frozen mango margarita and a savory olive-brine riff.
body: A great margarita is hard to beat: tequila, fresh lime juice, orange liqueur, and salt in sweet-tart harmony. But the classic margarita recipe is also an excellent starting point for experimentation. Small tweaks—swapping triple sec for agave syrup, say, or tequila for mezcal—can create a whole new drink. Perhaps even more compelling is the margarita's ability to veer into maximalism. Blend yours with frozen mango, muddle in fresh blackberries, or infuse the tequila with chiles.

Below you’ll find 19 of our best margarita recipes, including frozen margaritas, spicy margaritas, fruit-forward riffs, and a few less traditional variations. There’s a salted watermelon margarita for summer, a blood orange version for winter, and an avocado margarita that blends up remarkably creamy. Whether you like yours on the rocks, straight up, or frozen, there’s a margarita here for you.
points: Like spicy frozen mango margarita and a savory olive-brine riff.
